# Design Studio video: how it works, in detail

A preparation guide for teaching and demoing the Video pipeline. Every number here comes from runs in
your Design Studio history (Oct 4–6, 2026, Sora 2 version 2025-12-08 on `kestrel-ai`).

## 1. What the pipeline makes

**Every shot is a real video clip generated by Sora 2:** moving camera, moving subject, and its own
sound. Nothing is a slideshow of still images.

- A **keyframe** is a still image used only as the **first frame** of a product shot, so the car looks the
  same in every shot. Sora then animates from that frame.
- **Assembly** joins the clips you kept, in shot order. It adds a 0.5 s crossfade between clips, the visible
  label, and an optional 3 s end card. Nothing is generated at this step.

Round 1 *looked* like slides because the prompts asked for very little motion ("the car stays still",
"light sweeps"). Round 2 asked for specific actions, and the clips move. The difference came from the prompts,
not from the pipeline.

| Run in history | Shots | Median motion | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| SOLENNE GT · round 1 | 5 × 4 s, still-car prompts | 0.35 | "Looked like slides" |
| SOLENNE GT · family drive (round 2) | 4 × 8 s, action prompts | 2.02 | Usable ad, 30.5 s |

## 2. Two ways to start a video run

**Shot prompts** on the New video run form chooses between them.

| | Text model writes the shot list (default) | Off: one shot per line (prompt only) |
|---|---|---|
| You write | A brief: purpose, people, story, mood | One Sora prompt per line |
| Text model | gpt-6-astra turns the brief into shots with Sora-ready prompts | None |
| Keyframes | For product or scene shots, if you attach reference images | Never: every shot is text → video |
| What Sora receives | The model's prompt + sound cue + your "must not include" rules | **Your line, word for word** (plus "Keep it free of: …" only if you fill in Must not include) |
| Best for | Ads and stories with several shots and a consistent product | Learning Sora, testing one prompt, short clips |
| Example in history | *SOLENNE GT · 2-shot teaser*, *family drive* | *Prompt only · one 12-second clip* |

You review the shot list in both modes before any video is generated. That review step is where you fix
a prompt before paying for it.

## 3. The three ways a take is generated

| Mode | Label on the shot | Sora call | When it's used |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text → video | `text → video` | Prompt only | People shots, prompt-only runs, any run without references |
| Keyframe → video | `keyframe → video` | Prompt + the kept keyframe as the first frame | Product or scene shots when you attached a design sheet |
| Remix | "remix of s1_t2" | Changes one thing in an existing take | **Remix with a note** on a take |

Rules learned the hard way:

- **Sora rejects input images that contain human faces.** Shots with people are always text → video, so
  the app never sends a keyframe for them.
- **Sora remembers nothing between shots.** Each prompt must describe the subject fully: colour, shape,
  lights, clothing. That's why the shot-list instructions tell the text model to describe the subject in
  full in every shot.
- **Remix keeps the take and changes one thing.** Write only the change ("slower camera"). It only works
  while Sora still holds the original job, which is **24 hours**.

## 4. What happens behind one take

1. Design Studio sends `POST …/openai/v1/videos` with the model (`sora-2`), prompt, size (1280×720 or
   720×1280) and length (4, 8 or 12 s). Keyframe shots send the image as `input_reference`.
2. It saves Sora's job id **before** waiting, so a restart resumes the same job instead of paying again (test VD2).
3. It polls the job every few seconds; the take card shows *generating… n%*.
4. When done, it downloads the MP4 at once, because Sora deletes outputs after 24 hours.
5. It measures the clip (motion, audio, Content Credentials) and shows the take for your review.

| Clip length | Time per take (measured) |
|---|---|
| 4 s | about 55 s |
| 8 s | about 97 s |
| 12 s | about 140 s |

Two takes run at a time. If Sora answers "too many running tasks", the app waits for a slot and logs it.
The daily cap is 20 takes. **Sora 2 (2025-12-08) retires on Oct 15, 2026**; finished takes stay in history.

## 5. Automatic checks: what they measure and what they miss

| Check | How it's measured | What it can't tell you |
|---|---|---|
| Motion | Average brightness change between frames at 320×180 (0–255). Under 0.6 is flagged "may look like a still". | Whether the motion makes sense |
| Sound | ffmpeg volume and silence detection (gaps over 0.8 s) | Whether the sound fits. It's measured, not listened to |
| Content Credentials (C2PA) | `c2patool` on each raw take and on the final cut | Who made the edit you're watching |

**The lesson from the prompt-only run:** take 1 had the **highest** motion (7.05), but around 10 seconds
in the car drives onto the ocean and a badge-like emblem appears. Take 2 (5.39) follows the prompt and
stays on the road. A person watched both, rejected take 1 and kept take 2. A motion number measures change,
not physics.

Content Credentials:

- **Raw Sora takes** carry credentials, but they fail validation (`signingCredential.expired`): the vendor's
  certificate had expired.
- **The final cut has none**: re-encoding removes them. The burned-in label ("Made with AI") and the
  provenance report become the disclosure.

## 6. Assembly, step by step

1. Each kept take is trimmed to its length and scaled to the frame.
2. Clips are joined in shot order with a 0.5 s video and audio crossfade.
3. The visible label is drawn on every frame (top right).
4. If you set an end card, it follows the last clip with a 0.6 s fade and holds for about 3 s. The title
   is drawn by the app, so the spelling is exact.
5. An optional voiceover (MAI-Voice) is mixed over the takes' own sound, which plays at 45 %.
6. The cut is encoded as H.264 MP4. **Back to takes (re-cut)** lets you swap a take and assemble again;
   the earlier cut stays in history as superseded.

Example: two 4 s takes with an end card make 2 × 4 − 0.5 + 3 − 0.6 = **9.9 s** (the 2-shot teaser).

## 7. Writing prompts that move

1. **Name the subject fully in every prompt.** "A liquid-silver fictional electric grand tourer with thin white
   light bars", not "the car".
2. **Give it something to do.** Accelerates, turns, slows to a stop, a door opens. Avoid "stays still".
3. **Move the camera.** "Drone starts low beside the front wheel, rises and banks to follow from behind",
   "slow dolly in", "handheld from the back seat".
4. **Say what changes from the first second to the last.** Light, position, distance.
5. **Set light and place.** "Sunrise, coastal highway, rocky cliffs, breaking waves."
6. **Add one sound cue.** "Sound: wind rush and a soft rising synth." Sora generates the audio.
7. **One idea per clip.** Two events in 4 seconds rarely both happen.
8. **No real brands, logos, celebrities or readable plates.** The filters don't reliably stop them:
   the Ferrari test was not refused. The review checklist and the "must not include" rule are the real control.
9. **Fictional people only, by description.** Real faces can't be keyframes, and likeness needs consent.

Prompt-only line used in the reference run (12 s, sent to Sora as written):

> A liquid-silver fictional electric grand tourer with thin white light bars glides along a coastal highway at
> sunrise; a drone camera starts low beside the front wheel, rises and banks to follow from behind as the car
> accelerates past rocky cliffs and breaking waves, warm golden light flaring across the paint. Sound: wind
> rush and a soft rising synth.

## 8. Runs to study before class

| Run | What to look at |
|---|---|
| **Prompt only · one 12-second clip** | One line → Sora → two takes. Open both takes: the higher motion number is the wrong take. Read the reject note. |
| **SOLENNE GT · 2-shot teaser** | Shot 1 keyframe → video (design sheet), shot 2 text → video (person). Final 9.9 s cut with end card. |
| **SOLENNE GT · round 1** | 20 takes of still-car prompts; median motion 0.35. |
| **SOLENNE GT · family drive** | Fork of round 1 with action prompts; review notes on every take, including "car turns in a way a real car would not", "the model changed who is in the car", "design drift". |
| Compare round 1 vs family drive | Run history → tick both → **Compare 2 runs**: settings that changed next to results that changed. |
| Brand-name test (Restricted) | The vendor guardrail missed a real brand. Mac only; never exported. |

## 9. A 10-minute class demo

1. **Prompt only (3 min).** Open *Prompt only · one 12-second clip*. Read the line aloud, play both takes,
   ask the class which to keep, then show the motion numbers and the reject note.
2. **Why a pipeline (3 min).** Open *family drive*: the shot list, keyframes for the car, three takes per
   shot, and the notes on failed takes. Play the final cut.
3. **Before and after (2 min).** Compare round 1 vs family drive.
4. **Provenance (2 min).** On a take's review page, show *Content Credentials: present, fails check*; on
   the final cut, *none found*. The burned-in label is what survives.
5. **Optional live run:** a prompt-only 4 s clip (about 1 minute) from a student's line.

## 10. Words to use

- **Shot**: one planned clip in the ad.
- **Take**: one generation of a shot. You make several and keep one.
- **Keyframe**: the still image a product shot starts from.
- **Remix**: a new take that changes one thing in an existing take.
- **Cut**: the assembled video from the kept takes.
- **Review step** (*You review*): the run pauses until you approve.
